title: Rollforward timeline and hotseat checklist (personal scratch)
content:
Context: quick personal scratch to codify a tight rollforward plan and hotseat checklist for small-model flips or minor API shims. Meant to be handheld during the first 90 minutes of a live flip. Not a team runbook — use this to prompt the runbook and the slack thread.

High-level objective:
- Flip model/version or route policy, validate user-facing quality & latency, and be able to roll forward (not rollback) if early signals are green.
- Minimize blast radius and keep warm cohorts primed.

Pre-launch (T minus 90 to 0) — things I do personally:
- T-90: quick sanity check: verify canary image built + digest on staging (GH PR #842), infra tags present in registry. Note digest: sha256:<<<placeholder>>>.
- T-75: confirm warmup job completed for 3 anchor models in the canary pool (k8s job logs, job/warmup-canary-3).
- T-60: update release channel message in #deploys with expected timeline, contact list, and link to live metrics. Pin message.
- T-45: sanity curl to local canary endpoint with 3 golden prompts (latency + output sanity). Example:
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN' 
    -d '{"model":"open-llm:2.1.3-canary","input":"<golden-short>","max_tokens":32}' 

  Expect: 200 + output contains expected anchor phrase + p50 latency < 120ms in my region.
- T-30: confirm dashboards: per-route latency, token-cost rate, error-rate, regenerations. Open these in a browser window:
  - Console route dashboard: /console/routes/anchors
  - Trace sampler: /console/traces?filter=canary
  - Eval-run outputs: /console/evals/rollforward-smoke
- T-10: put phone on DND to reduce noise, ensure hotseat slack DMs are reachable.

Minute-by-minute (launch, 0 to +30):
- 0m: flip traffic fraction: 1% -> 5% (rollforward cadence: 1% increments up to 10% in first 10 min). Use API or SDK:
  # sample SDK (python)
  from redwood import Client
  c = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
  c.routes.update('prod-main', traffic_rules=[{'model':'open-llm:2.1.3-canary','fraction':0.05}])
- 0-2m: sanity checks for immediate 5% cohort:
  - p95 latency <= baseline * 1.25
  - error rate (5xx + 4xx from canary cohort) < 0.5% absolute increase
  - quality smoke: 3 golden prompts produce expected anchors (human view)
- 3-6m: bump to 10% if green. Record exact timestamps and who bumped. Annotate slack thread with traffic changes and key metric snapshots.
- 6-15m: hold at 10% and watch for regression signals:
  - regressions to watch: hallucination-score spike (eval-based), prompt truncation rate, request queue depth on canary nodes, memory GC spikes on GPUs.
  - telemetry check commands (my local quickies):
    kubectl top pods -l canary=true -n serving
    curl https://metrics.internal/api?query=canary_latency_p95
- 15-30m: if stable, proceed to 25-30% then 50% during off-peak windows. If any signal trips (see thresholds below) then STOP and engage emergency plan.

Thresholds that make me halt and hold or roll back immediately:
- sustained p95 latency > baseline * 1.5 for >5m
- error rate delta >= 1.5% absolute for any 5m window
- new OOM or eviction events on canary nodes
- eval-based quality regressions: model-specific BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim drop > 6% on the smoke set
- any customer-facing complaint flagged by CS that is traced to the canary cohort

Hotseat checklist (people + comms) — who I DM first if something bad shows:
- Primary on-call: Rae Chen (pager + phone)
- Backup on-call: Miguel Santos
- Product contact: Anika Patel (for customer comms)
- CS on-call: cs-urgent@redwood.ai (or ping #cs-urgent)
- Pager: PG-ops channel and schedule link in Confluence (link above)

Emergency quick rollback (if needed) — shorthand steps I keep handy:
- Step 1: freeze traffic (set fraction to 0% for canary model):
  c.routes.update('prod-main', traffic_rules=[{'model':'open-llm:2.1.3-canary','fraction':0}])
- Step 2: switch route to previous pinned model version and confirm token use:
  c.routes.update('prod-main', traffic_rules=[{'model':'open-llm:2.1.2-stable','fraction':1.0}])
- Step 3: post-mortem note skeleton: immediate incident timeline, stack traces, sample failing requests, mitigations applied, next steps. Create Incident INF-2147 in Linear and assign.

Post-launch (30m to 6h) — short-term observations I take:
- 30-90m: keep annotated list of sample failures and inputs in the slack thread; capture 10 representative failing inputs.
- 2-6h: check longer-term quality signals (user engagement, downstream rerank recalls, business KPI proxies). If OK, continue progressive roll to 100% per agreed cadence.

Personal heuristics and micro-notes (why I prefer rollforward cadence above):
- small increments let me see slow degradations that a single big flip would hide.
- keep warm caches hot: issue synthetic warm requests to canary nodes every 20s for first 15m to avoid cold-cache variance. Implement with a small script.
- prefer rollforward (increase fraction) over immediate rollback when small noisy spikes appear, but only when errors are transient and isolated. If systemic, then rollback.

Commands/snippets I scribble during runs:
- snapshot current route config: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/prod-main
- set fractional traffic (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/prod-main/update \\n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n    -d '{"traffic_rules":[{"model":"open-llm:2.1.3-canary","fraction":0.05}]}'
- warmup runner (bash):
  PVTS=10; for i in $(seq 1 $PVTS); do curl -s -X POST https://canary.local/warm -d '{"prompt":"<anchor>"}' & done

Open questions / TODOs for follow-up:
- Add a telemetry alert that flags embedding-similarity shift for 3 golden prompts (INF telemetry ticket?)
- Add a one-click rollback button to the console route page for canary model (UX request filed in #platform-ux).
- Validate that canary nodes are attached to distinct failure domains to avoid colocation risk.

Scratch log (what I did last time, quick notes):
- 2025-01-08 09:12 UTC — flipped 1% -> 5%: minute 4 latency spike due to garbage collection; held and then proceeded after GC cooled.
- 2025-01-08 09:28 UTC — found a weird truncation on long prompts; added prompt-length guard in SDK (client-side) for 1.2% of requests.

End-of-note: this is my personal operating scratch for rollforwards. Copy into team runbook if it stabilizes. Keep short, keep actionable.

-- PN
